findings.title: Password verification can be bypassed when logging in with a backup code
findings.body: On line 121, password verification is guarded by `if (user.password && !credentials.totpCode)`, while line 131 checks `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` before the `else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)` TOTP branch. If a request to the credentials provider includes both a `backupCode` and any non-empty `totpCode` string (e.g. `totpCode: "1"`), line 121 is skipped so `verifyPassword` is never executed, and line 131 enters the backup-code branch so `totpCode` is never validated either. This allows an attacker who obtains or brute-forces a backup code to log in as a user (or probe whether backup codes exist/match) without knowing the user's password. Additionally, lines 113 and 117 only check `!credentials.totpCode` (and `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` line 180 renders `ExternalTotpFooter` instead of `TwoFactorFooter` when `totpEmail` is set), so third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes at all.

findings.title: Dismissing the modal on the backup codes step leaves UI state out of sync and does not reset form state
findings.body: In `handleEnable`, `onEnable()` was replaced with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)`, and `onEnable()` + `resetState()` are now only invoked when the user clicks the `[data-testid="backup-codes-close"]` button (lines 266-270). If the user closes the modal on the backup codes screen via the dialog's `X` button, clicking the backdrop, or pressing `Escape` (which triggers `onOpenChange` on line 166), neither `onEnable()` nor `resetState()` is called—leaving the 2FA switch in the parent settings page unchecked even though 2FA is already enabled in the database, and leaving `step` stuck on `DisplayBackupCodes` if the modal is reopened. In addition, `resetState()` (lines 71-75) does not call `form.reset()` (or clear `totpCode`), so `totpCode` retains the previous 6-digit value if the modal is used again in the same session.

findings.title: First 2FA E2E test does not complete the backup-codes step and passes due to an unawaited Promise assertion
findings.body: In the first test (`"should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA"`), after `fillOtp` enters the TOTP digits, the modal now transitions to the backup codes step (`SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes`) rather than immediately calling `onEnable()`. Unlike the second test (lines 110-127), this test never waits for the backup codes step or clicks `backup-codes-close`. Line 53 (`await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`) only passes because `isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` and `expect(promise).toBeTruthy()` checks that the `Promise` object itself is truthy without awaiting it. Because neither the enable API response nor the backup codes modal is awaited after `fillOtp`'s async auto-submit, the test immediately navigates to `/auth/logout` on line 59, racing with the in-flight `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable` request.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code on the login page fails silently with no error message
findings.body: The login `<form>` on line 188 sets `noValidate`, which disables native HTML validation for the `required` and `minLength={10}` attributes on `<BackupCode />`, and `formSchema` (lines 57-66) uses `.passthrough()` without validating `backupCode`. If a user on the backup code step submits the form with an empty backup code, `next-auth-options.ts` skips `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode)` (since `backupCode` is `""`) and throws `ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired`. On line 156, `res.error === ErrorCode.SecondFactorRequired` only calls `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` (which is already `true`) and sets no error message, so the submission fails silently with no feedback to the user.
